samples.summary: Increase/Decrease decimals now scans every populated cell of a column/row/whole-sheet selection, defeating the layer-level fast path those selections were built on
samples.evidence: `setRangeStyle`'s contract (sheet.ts:3723-3727 and docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:69-77) is that column/row/all selections write ONE style at the column/row/sheet layer "instead of iterating every cell". `changeDecimals` (sheet.ts:4315) now routes those same selections through `selectionRendersAt` (sheet.ts:4376 `await this.store.getGrid(range)`), `unsetKeepsRendering` (sheet.ts:4420) and `unsetRangeStyleValues` (sheet.ts:4545-4554, one `await this.store.get(anchor)` per populated cell). For `selectAllCells()` (sheet.ts:3012) the range is the whole dimension, so a single toolbar click on a large sheet now does O(populated cells) sequential awaits against `YorkieStore` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:445) where it previously did one `setSheetStyle`. Note the codebase already caps comparable whole-selection loops (`MaxBorderSelectionCells` in `setRangeBorders`, `MaxCheckboxToggleCells`); the new paths have no cap. Fix belongs on the new code (bound the scan, or skip it for column/row/all selections).

samples.summary: `defaultKeys` pinning materialises an INHERITED `nf` as an explicit cell-level style, permanently detaching those cells from their column/row/sheet format
samples.evidence: `collectStyleValuesToPin` reads the *effective* style (sheet.ts:3836, which merges sheet→col→row→range layers via `resolveEffectiveStyle`, sheet.ts:912) and then writes it back with `await this.setStyle(parseRef(sref), keep)` (sheet.ts:3803). A cell that merely inherited `nf: 'percent'` from a column style now stores `nf: 'percent'` on itself. Every later layer-level format change is silently ignored for those cells: `setRangeStyle` on a column writes `colStyles` (sheet.ts:3750) and `resolveEffectiveStyle` gives cell-level keys the highest precedence, so a subsequent "Format as percent/currency" applied to that column will no longer reach any cell a decimal step touched. It also creates cell-level style payloads (and CRDT nodes) for cells that previously had none. The test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:596-612 pins the pinning behaviour but not this consequence.

samples.summary: `isEmptyCell` was not updated alongside `compactCell`, so a spill ghost whose style becomes empty is still deleted and loses the `spillAnchor` the change set out to preserve
samples.evidence: `compactCell` now carries `spillRows/spillCols/spillAnchor/spillBlocked` (style-mutation.ts:69-80), but `isEmptyCell` (style-mutation.ts:48-52) still judges emptiness on value/formula/style only. Spill ghosts are written as `{ v: values[dr][dc] ?? '', spillAnchor: sref }` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:141), so a ghost holding an empty string whose style is emptied hits `isEmptyCell` → `store.delete` in `setStyle` (sheet.ts:3716-3719) and in `unsetRangeStyleValues` (sheet.ts:4632-4635), dropping the anchor link the calculator reads at calculator.ts:80 and calculator.ts:109. The preservation the diff adds therefore does not hold on the paths this same change introduces.

samples.summary: Dropping `dp` from `DefaultStyleValues` means `dp: 2` now survives in range patches, so patches that used to prune/merge no longer collapse
samples.evidence: `DefaultStyleValues` is consumed only by `pruneRedundantDefaultStyleKeys` (style-mutation.ts:274-311), which `addRangeStylePatch` (sheet.ts:1894, 1916) uses to drop no-op keys and to delete a tail patch that becomes fully redundant. With `dp` removed, any patch carrying `dp: 2` — which the xlsx importer emits liberally (packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-styles.ts:229, 239, 243, 250, 252) and which the toolbar can now write — keeps the key, so `stylesEqual`/`tryMergeRangeStylePatches` (style-mutation.ts:131-183) stop collapsing otherwise-identical patches and the persisted `rangeStyles` list grows. The trade-off is documented (docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:276), but the patch-count/document-size effect on the import and toolbar paths is not.

samples.summary: `getActiveDecimalPlaces` is now public API with no consumer left anywhere in the repo
samples.evidence: `packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:533-547` was the last decimal-state consumer and now calls `sheet.changeDecimals()` only. A repo-wide grep for `getActiveDecimalPlaces` finds it solely at its definition (sheet.ts:4254) and in docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md; nothing in packages/frontend, cli, or the sheets tests calls it. It was updated to clamp in this change, so it reads as live API while being dead.

verdict.reason: The code exists roughly as quoted, but it is not a blast-radius defect. Repo-wide grep for `unsetRangeStyleValues|selectionRendersAt|unsetKeepsRendering` yields matches only inside packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts (:4318, :4335, :4346, :4374, :4414, :4472) — no consumer in any other module or package. `setRangeStyle`'s contract is untouched: its column/row/all layer fast paths still return early exactly as before (sheet.ts:3739-3784), so no existing caller is broken, no guard is bypassed, no export removed/renamed, no signature or return shape changed for anyone. The complaint is purely about the cost of the new function's own loops — statable without leaving the diff, and the reviewer concedes the fix belongs on the new code — which the rubric assigns to the correctness lens, not this one. The claimed severity analogy is also inapt: MaxBorderSelectionCells (sheet.ts:4057-4062) and MaxCheckboxToggleCells (sheet.ts:3987-3995) cap loops that walk every coordinate of the rectangle, whereas the new scans go through store.getGrid, which iterates only populated cells via CellIndex.cellsInRange (packages/sheets/src/store/cell-index.ts:82-96) and reads from an in-memory index/doc (yorkie-store.ts:445-466, :295-302) — the same populated-cell scan the pre-existing setRangeStyle cell path already performs uncapped (sheet.ts:3795-3801), and which the repo's own lesson doc treats as the acceptable bound (docs/tasks/archive/2026/07/20260712-checkbox-parity-lessons.md:24-26).

finding.summary: `defaultKeys` pinning materialises an INHERITED `nf` as an explicit cell-level style, permanently detaching those cells from their column/row/sheet format
finding.evidence: `collectStyleValuesToPin` reads the *effective* style (sheet.ts:3836, which merges sheet→col→row→range layers via `resolveEffectiveStyle`, sheet.ts:912) and then writes it back with `await this.setStyle(parseRef(sref), keep)` (sheet.ts:3803). A cell that merely inherited `nf: 'percent'` from a column style now stores `nf: 'percent'` on itself. Every later layer-level format change is silently ignored for those cells: `setRangeStyle` on a column writes `colStyles` (sheet.ts:3750) and `resolveEffectiveStyle` gives cell-level keys the highest precedence, so a subsequent "Format as percent/currency" applied to that column will no longer reach any cell a decimal step touched. It also creates cell-level style payloads (and CRDT nodes) for cells that previously had none. The test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:596-612 pins the pinning behaviour but not this consequence.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `collectStyleValuesToPin` (sheet.ts:3818-3850) reads the merged/effective style via `resolveEffectiveStyle` at sheet.ts:3836 — not the cell's own `cell.s` — and copies each `defaultKeys` value into `keep` (3843); `setRangeStyle` then persists it as an explicit cell-level style through `setStyle` at sheet.ts:3803 (setStyle merges into `cell.s` and writes, 3705-3721). `compactCell` (style-mutation.ts:61-85) does no de-duplication against inherited layers, so cells that previously had no `s` now carry one. Because `resolveEffectiveStyle` gives cell-level keys top precedence (`{...s, ...c, ...r, ...range, ...cellStyle}`, sheet.ts:917), a later column-selection format write, which only touches `colStyles`/`store.setColumnStyle` (sheet.ts:3742-3751), is shadowed for every pinned cell. This is a genuine behaviour change relative to the surrounding contract: the pre-existing `applyStylePatchToExistingCells` deliberately only touches keys the cell already owned (`if (prev === undefined || prev === next) continue;`, sheet.ts:2009). The path is reachable from `changeDecimals` (sheet.ts:4352-4359) and is covered by the test at decimals.test.ts:596-612, which asserts only the rendering, not the absence of the newly materialised cell-level style. `resetRangeStyleToDefault` (3856-3875) can clear cell styles, so "permanently" is mildly overstated, but nothing guards the shadowing itself, so no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: The new `clampDecimals` guard only covers the render path; the step/write path still reads an untrusted stored `dp` unclamped
finding.evidence: `clampDecimals` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/format.ts:22) is introduced precisely because "a `dp` can come from anywhere a style can — an imported `.xlsx`, a collaborator's document". But the write path never passes through it: `getActiveDecimalState` returns `style.dp` raw (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4184), `changeDecimals` does arithmetic on that raw value (`Math.min(dp + delta, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES)`, sheet.ts:4202) and then stores the result (`setRangeStyle({ dp: target })`, sheet.ts:4236) and also uses it as the unset match value (`{ dp, nf }`, sheet.ts:4230). A stored non-integer/non-number `dp` therefore round-trips back into the shared document: a `dp` of `"3"` from a peer or import makes `dp + delta` string-concatenate to `"31"`, which is then written as the new `dp`; a fractional `dp` of 2.5 is stored as 3.5. `getActiveDecimalPlaces` (sheet.ts:4156) likewise hands `style?.dp ?? 2` to callers unclamped. Fix belongs on the new code: clamp in `getActiveDecimalState`/`changeDecimals` before stepping, not only inside `formatValue`.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the step/write path reads a stored `dp` unclamped, but the code is not as described. `getActiveDecimalState` returns `dp: clampDecimals(style.dp, rendersRaw ? valueDp : 2)` (sheet.ts:4295), not raw `style.dp`; `getActiveDecimalPlaces` returns `clampDecimals(style?.dp, 2)` (sheet.ts:4256), not `style?.dp ?? 2`. `changeDecimals` destructures `dp` from the already-clamped `getActiveDecimalState()` (sheet.ts:4316) before doing `Math.min(dp + delta, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES)` (sheet.ts:4317), so both the unset match value `{ dp, nf }` (sheet.ts:4345) and the stored patch `{ dp: target }` (sheet.ts:4351) derive from the clamped value. Every line number cited by the reviewer (4156, 4184, 4202, 4230, 4236) belongs to unrelated merge code (`mergeSelection`, sheet.ts:4159-4188, 4201-4204; merge deletion loop 4230-4238). The concrete round-trip scenarios also fail: `clampDecimals` (format.ts:22-30) rejects a non-number `"3"` via `Number.isFinite` and returns the fallback (no `"31"` concatenation), and truncates `2.5` to `2` (no `3.5` write). The only other stored-`dp` reads in sheet.ts (1000, 4859) flow into `formatValue`, which clamps at format.ts:191 and format.ts:213. No unclamped write path exists.

finding.summary: `renderedDecimals` hardcodes 2 decimals for a `dp`-less currency format, contradicting `formatValue`'s currency branch for non-2-digit currencies (KRW, JPY, KWD)
finding.evidence: `renderedDecimals` returns `clampDecimals(style?.dp, 2)` for every numeric format (format.ts:160), but `formatValue` deliberately omits the fraction-digit options for currency when `dp === undefined` (format.ts:198-203) so Intl applies the *currency's own* default: 0 for KRW/JPY, 3 for KWD. `resolveCurrencyForLocale` maps KR→KRW and JP→JPY (packages/sheets/src/model/core/locale.ts:47,49), so this is a routine document, not an exotic one. `selectionRendersAt` (sheet.ts:4263) now decides the Decrease no-op through `renderedDecimals`, so a KRW/JPY currency cell that actually renders 0 decimals reports 2, the whole-selection no-op guard is defeated, and Decrease writes an explicit `{dp: 0}` residue onto neighbours that had no style at all — the exact residue the feature exists to avoid. docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:257 repeats the same wrong assumption ("an absent `dp` means the *format's* default of 2").

verdict.reason: The central premise is factually absent from the repo. `renderedDecimals` does NOT hardcode 2 for a dp-less currency: format.ts:184-190 branches on `nf === 'currency' && style?.dp === undefined` and delegates to `currencyDecimals` (format.ts:149-161), which reads `Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {style:'currency', currency}).resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits` — the currency's own convention (0 for KRW/JPY, 3 for KWD). The `clampDecimals(style?.dp, 2)` at format.ts:191 is only reached for non-currency formats or a currency that stores an explicit `dp`, which is exactly what `formatValue`'s currency branch does (format.ts:229-240: options omitted when `dp === undefined`, explicit min/max when set). The `2` the reviewer cites as "format.ts:160" is the catch-fallback inside `currencyDecimals`, matching `safeFormat`'s degradation chain (format.ts:50-59). The claimed downstream breakage therefore does not occur: `selectionRendersAt` (sheet.ts:4374-4394) forwards the cell's own currency at sheet.ts:4386 (`{ currency: effective?.cu }`), so a KRW/JPY cell reports 0, the whole-selection no-op guard at sheet.ts:4318 fires, and no `{dp: 0}` residue is written. The doc citation is also wrong in location and contradicted in the same file: the "format's default of 2" prose is at docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:258, while :315-319 explicitly documents the correct currency-convention behaviour including KRW/JPY/KWD; that residual prose imprecision is a doc nit, not a broken caller or bypassed guard, and is out of scope for the blast-radius rubric. Tests at packages/sheets/test/model/format.test.ts:229-251 cover the currency branch.
